blogs.title: The Triple Threat: Navigating Feasibility and Planning in 'TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV' Procedures
blogs.description: As TAVI populations age and survive longer, the era of the third-generation transcatheter valve is arriving sooner than expected. This post breaks down the specific anatomical constraints of stacking three devices, focusing on how pre-procedural CT modeling is critical for assessing frame-layering interactions, calculating the remaining effective orifice area (EOA), and determining if a patient has enough room for another stint before becoming a surgical candidate.

blogs.title: To Cut or Not to Cut? Managing Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis After Multiple Prior TAVIs
blogs.description: Standard guidelines favor surgery for Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis (PVE), yet this patient with prohibitive EuroSCORE II (>27%) successfully underwent a third TAVI after treated PVE. We analyze the shifting paradigm where 'active infection' becomes less absolute than 'anatomical feasibility,' discussing how multidisciplinary teams weigh the risks of emergent complex aortic root replacement versus controlled elective intervention after antibiotics.

blogs.title: High Stakes Landing Zones: Mitigating Coronary Obstruction in Sequential Re-interventions
blogs.description: With every added valve frame, the risk of creating a 'neo-skirt' that blocks coronary flow increases exponentially. Using this case as a blueprint, we explore advanced CT metrics like valve-to-coronary distance and sinus dimensions. The post details why high-implantation strategies were chosen here to push the new leaflets above the coronaries and discusses whether techniques like BASILICA remain viable options in a triple-stented environment.

blogs.title: Resolving Patient-Prosthesis Mismatch: Why Gradient Normalization Took Time Post-PMEC
blogs.description: Immediately post-procedure, this patient exhibited severe patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) despite technical success, only resolving over several months. This blog dissects the hemodynamics of 'stacked' valves, explaining why acute gradients can be misleading in complex anatomy. We discuss the roles of frame friction, incomplete radial force expansion of inner layers, and how aggressive balloon post-dilation facilitates delayed remodeling and improved effective orifice areas.

blogs.title: Lifetime Management: Commissural Alignment as a Lifeline for Future Coronary Access
blogs.description: In a world where these patients will inevitably require future PCI or CABG, does valve orientation matter now? This article examines the strategic decision to align commissures during TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV implantation. We review the evidence suggesting that maintaining clear pathways through dense metallic lattices is crucial for surviving not just one failure event, but potentially multiple life-cycle stages in modern structural heart disease care.
